headword: お{弁当|べんとう}{温|あたた}め

definitions.gloss: bento heating service; warming up boxed meals
definitions.explanation: A service offered at convenience stores where staff will heat up your purchased bento or food items in a microwave.

examples.japanese: お{弁当|べんとう}、{温|あたた}めますか？
examples.english: Would you like me to heat up your bento?
examples.notes: Standard question from convenience store staff

examples.japanese: お{弁当|べんとう}{温|あたた}めは{結構|けっこう}です。
examples.english: I don't need the bento heated, thanks.

examples.japanese: コンビニでお{弁当|べんとう}を{買|か}ったら{温|あたた}めてもらえる。
examples.english: When you buy a bento at a convenience store, they can heat it up for you.

notes:
お{弁当|べんとう}{温|あたた}め refers to the free microwave heating service at Japanese convenience stores. When buying a {弁当|べんとう} or similar prepared food, the cashier will typically ask if you want it heated.

COMMON EXCHANGE:
- {店員|てんいん}: 「お{弁当|べんとう}、{温|あたた}めますか？」(Shall I heat your bento?)
- To accept: 「お{願|ねが}いします」(Yes, please)
- To decline: 「{結構|けっこう}です」(No, thank you) or 「{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です」(I'm fine)

CULTURAL NOTE:
This question is one of the first set phrases visitors to Japan encounter at convenience stores, along with 「レジ{袋|ぶくろ}はいりますか」(Do you need a plastic bag?) and 「ポイントカードはありますか」(Do you have a point card?).

NOTE:
Some items have specific heating times printed on the packaging. The service is free and standard at all major convenience store chains.
